rules.name: Poset antisymmetry seed
rules.input_form: binary relation on a carrier set
rules.output_form: partial-order structure when reflexive, antisymmetric, and transitive
preconditions: A carrier set and comparison relation are fixed
rules.operation: Recognize a partial order through reflexivity, antisymmetry, and transitivity.
examples: Subset inclusion on a power set defines a standard partial order
counterexamples: A relation with cycles between distinct elements violates antisymmetry

rules.name: Galois connection seed
rules.input_form: paired monotone maps between ordered sets
preconditions: The ordered sets and monotone maps are fixed
rules.operation: Use equivalent inequality conditions to recognize a Galois connection.
examples: Closure-style constructions often arise from paired order-reversing or order-preserving adjoint behavior
counterexamples: Unrelated monotone maps do not automatically define a Galois connection

rules.name: Field extension degree seed
rules.input_form: tower of finite field extensions
preconditions: A finite tower of fields is fixed
rules.operation: Multiply intermediate degrees to obtain the total extension degree.
examples: Extension size in a tower can be decomposed into successive intermediate degrees
counterexamples: Treating arbitrary nonfield extensions as if degree multiplicativity automatically applies is invalid

rules.name: Minimal polynomial seed
rules.input_form: algebraic element over a base field
preconditions: The element is algebraic over the base field
rules.operation: Encode algebraic dependence by the unique monic polynomial of least degree that vanishes at the element.
examples: Algebraic dependence over a base field is encoded by the minimal polynomial relation
counterexamples: Transcendental elements do not possess minimal polynomials over the base field

rules.name: Non-associative closure seed
rules.input_form: bilinear product on a vector space or module-like object
preconditions: Closure and bilinearity are fixed for the product
rules.operation: Allow algebraic multiplication without imposing associativity.
examples: Lie and Jordan algebras are algebraic systems whose multiplication laws are not governed by ordinary associativity
counterexamples: Assuming every bilinear product is associative erases genuine non-associative structure

rules.name: Jordan identity seed
rules.input_form: commutative non-associative product
rules.output_form: Jordan-algebra structure when the Jordan identity holds
preconditions: A commutative bilinear product is fixed
rules.operation: Recognize Jordan structure through the Jordan identity rather than associativity.
examples: Symmetric operator products motivate Jordan-type algebraic structures distinct from associative multiplication
counterexamples: Any commutative bilinear product lacking the Jordan identity is not automatically a Jordan algebra

rules.name: Complete lattice seed
rules.input_form: partially ordered set with arbitrary subset bounds
preconditions: Arbitrary subset joins and meets are defined in the active order
rules.operation: Recognize completeness by existence of joins and meets for arbitrary subsets.
examples: Power sets ordered by inclusion form complete lattices through unions and intersections
counterexamples: A finite-join structure without arbitrary subset bounds is not automatically complete

rules.name: Galois correspondence seed
rules.input_form: finite Galois extension with automorphism group data
rules.output_form: order-reversing correspondence between intermediate fields and subgroups
preconditions: A finite Galois extension and its automorphism group are fixed
rules.operation: Relate intermediate fields to automorphism subgroups through the classical correspondence.
examples: Intermediate fields and automorphism subgroups are matched through a structural correspondence rather than by arbitrary enumeration
counterexamples: Arbitrary extensions without the required normal-separable hypotheses do not automatically satisfy the classical correspondence

rules.name: Alternative algebra seed
rules.input_form: nonassociative product with left- and right-alternative laws
preconditions: A bilinear product and active alternative identities are fixed
rules.operation: Weaken associativity by imposing the alternative laws instead of full associativity.
examples: Octonion multiplication is nonassociative but still alternative
counterexamples: A nonassociative product with no left- or right-alternative law is not automatically alternative

rules.name: Octonion norm seed

rules.operation: Preserve norm multiplicativity despite nonassociative multiplication.
examples: Norm multiplicativity allows inverse and magnitude control despite nonassociative multiplication
